text:
maria-sec: runtime scanner flagged a container on node-12 mounting /proc and /run/secrets via hostPath. possible access to instance metadata and mounted service account tokens. alert id: RUNTIME-2026-03-20-01

jordan-sre: ack. can we confirm if this is an initContainer or main container? any image digest?

maria-sec: it appears to be a sidecar. image: registry.redwood-inference/internal/metrics-sidecar:sha256:4f3b2... config shows hostPath: /var/run/host_proc -> /proc and /var/run/secrets -> /run/secrets

devon-runtime: cordon node-12 now? also we should evict non-critical pods and isolate egress to metadata service.

sam-ops: cordoning + drain in progress. running: `kubectl cordon node-12 && kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

leo-forensics: copying container logs and filesystem snapshot before pod is force-removed. storing under s3://forensics/node-12/1924567890/ . pulling `tar -czf /tmp/sidecar-snapshot.tar.gz /proc /run/secrets` from container runtime.

alex-platform: if credentials were exposed we need KMS rotation plan and service account token revocation. also check whether any ClusterRoleBindings were changed recently.

sec-bot: automated alert: suspicious hostPath usage detected; policy=hostpath-disallow, severity=high. related events: 2026-03-20T01:03:12Z pod-create, 2026-03-20T01:03:14Z mount-hostpath

ci-bot: deployment pipeline 2891 just finished for metrics-sidecar -> commit abc123. user: eng-ci-bot. no manual approvals.

jordan-sre: can someone grep audit logs for `kubectl create` and `ClusterRoleBinding` around +24h window? my hunch: this was a misconfigured helm chart but we must assume compromise until proven otherwise.

maria-sec: grep answers: no recent ClusterRoleBinding changes by human users. there is one automated job that updated a Role in namespace infra last week. we should still treat tokens as possibly exfiltrated.

devon-runtime: immediate mitigation checklist: 1) isolate node network egress to metadata (iptables rule applied) 2) rotate KMS keys for infra secrets used by that namespace 3) revoke service account tokens and recreate secrets 4) rollback metrics-sidecar to previous signed digest and remove hostPath in manifest

sam-ops: applied iptables block on node-12 to 169.254.169.254: `iptables -A OUTPUT -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP`

leo-forensics: snapshot uploaded. starting binary diffs and file hash comparisons against golden image. will check if any suid/extra binaries were dropped.

alex-platform: about RBAC: schedule an emergency policy change to block `hostPath` in admission controller with OPA gate, and add a deny policy for `mountPath` to `/proc` and `/run/secrets`. we should also disallow `hostNetwork` for non-system namespaces until review.

maria-sec: agreed. opening ticket INFRA-4267 for emergency PSA + OPA rule. also adding audit-alert rule for any future hostPath mounts.

jordan-sre: for containment complete steps: node cordoned/drained, sidecar pods terminated, image pulled removed from registry tag pointing to digest rollback. confirm registry signed image check: `cosign verify --key k8s/cosign.pub registry.../metrics-sidecar@sha256:4f3b2...`

devon-runtime: cosign verify failed on that digest (signature mismatch). we pulled the previous known-good digest (sha256:9a8c7...) and redeployed without hostPath. rollback applied.

maria-sec: KMS rotation: triggered customer-managed KMS key rotation for infra-secrets. also rotated CI service principal keys and revoked long-lived tokens for namespace infra. documented emails sent to oncall and security leads.

leo-forensics: evidence so far: no outbound connections from the sidecar other than the registry and telemetry host; no immediate signs of exfil to external IPs. we still found reads of `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` in process open files.

alex-platform: followups: 1) force recreate all service account secrets in prod 2) add audit retention + search indexing for hostPath events 3) ship an OPA deny policy ASAP 4) rotate keys and verify KMS access logs for any unusual decrypts in the last 48h

maria-sec: agreed. owners: devon-runtime -> OPA rule & admission change, jordan-sre -> audit log search & retention, sam-ops -> token rotation runbook, leo-forensics -> final report + hashes, alex-platform -> registry hardening and cosign enforcement. due date: EOD tomorrow for containment and rotation, full postmortem in 48h.

sec-bot: incident severity set to P2. creating incident channel #incident-runtime-node12-1924567890.

jordan-sre: note for post-incident: evaluate service account issuer config, ensure `BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume` and short TTLs, enable K8s audit policy `requestBody` for create/update on pods.

maria-sec: adding checklist to INFRA-4267 and creating followup ticket for long-term mitigations: tighten admission, enforce cosign verify in CI, ban hostPath usage in app charts, and add runtime detection for process reads of serviceaccount tokens.

sam-ops: all containment actions completed per checklist. leaving node-12 offline until forensics thumbs-up. will update on channel when node is back. :white_check_mark:
